section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1982
title: Causes of Accidental Deaths The total accidental deaths recorded during 1982 have been classified under two broad categories: (A). Accidental Death due to natural causes like lighting, heat strokes, floods, land slides, cold and exposure and cyclone, and (B) Accidental deaths due to other causes like mishaps in factoreis, road accidents, air crashes, house collapse and boat capsizing. Category (A) accounted for 3 · 6 per cent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1982 in comparison to 3 · 3 percent in 1981. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths in 1982 were due to ‘Lightning’ (1754) followed by ‘Floods’ (699) ‘Land Slides’ (596), ‘Cyclone’ (505), ‘Heat Strokes’ (492) and ‘Cold & Exposure’ (391). Category (B) claimed 96 · 4 per cent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1982 as against 96 · 7 per cent registered during 1981. Under this category, the highest number of accidental deaths in 1982 was recorded under the head ‘By Drowning’ (22,632), followed by ‘Accidental Death on Roads (22,199), ‘By Fire’ (14,555), ‘In Railways’ (12,789), ‘By poisoning’ (6,846), ‘By snake biting’ (3,299), ‘By fire arms (1,874) ‘By animal biting/killing’ (1,437), ‘By house collapse’ (1,157), ‘In factoreis’ (735), ‘In mines and Quarry Disaster (624), By explosion (356), ‘By boat capsize’ (161) and in ‘Air crashes’ (102). The Miscellaneous causes’ recorded a total number of 32,790 accidental death cases during 1982 as against 31,827 cases in 1981 sharing 26 · 0 per cent of the total accidental deaths. During 1982 ‘Drowning’ accounted for 18 · 0 per cent of the total accidents in India followed by ‘Accidental Death on Roads’ (17 · 6%), ‘By Fire’ (11 · 6%) and in ‘Railways’ (10 · 1%). notes: Incidence of Accidental Deaths in the States/Union Territories and Metropolitan Cities

The incidence of accidental deaths in all the States taken together recorded an increase of 2.8 per cent in 1982 over 1981.
